policy_findings.rationale: The phase removes an enforcement path, so the rule's concern (a failure or uncertain state represented as success) is live — but every non-success state it touches stays visible with a safe next action. Unparseable/missing/unreadable config still fails the transaction with CONFIG_INVALID and still yields a `config-invalid` blocker plus an `inspect-state` (`human_required: true`) action naming the file and the read issue. The legacy fingerprint fallback retries exactly once and, on double mismatch, lets the existing mismatch error fire unchanged. The two places where the system deliberately says nothing — pre-cutover tasks with no `last_seen_config`, and settlement commits that never read config — are stated plainly, their honest reading is argued ("the notice persists until the next config-observing commit"), and both are pinned by named integration assertions rather than left implicit. The `ConfigVerification` surface keeps `{verified, issue?}`, so an unverifiable config is still reported as such.

policy_findings.rationale: Changing the fingerprint composition and adding an acceptance fallback touches the machinery that binds evidence to subject bytes, so the rule is engaged. The fallback is bounded and does not weaken failing closed: it is a single retry under the pre-change field set with `config_digest` taken from the recorded creation-time `state.config_digest` (never live bytes, verified as the value the pin guaranteed at recording time), it never rewrites a recorded value, and a double mismatch still errors. Task and subject identity are untouched — `TaskStateV1.config_digest` provenance and its state-vs-initialization and receipt-vs-prepared-state agreement checks (`src/contracts/durable.ts:713-714`, `:796-798`) remain, `assertPreserved` still pins the digest as substrate, and reentry evidence continuity continues to ride the recorded predecessor-fingerprint pair. Config bytes do leave the evidence binding, but that is exactly PRD R1 and design D2, and per-dispatch route provenance remains the durable record of what ran. The `last_seen_config` write is placed inside `buildPlan` before `prepared_state`/`prepared_state_digest` derivation so committed bytes, receipt, and crash replay cannot disagree — i.e. no partial or self-inconsistent durable record is introduced.

Retry-once-and-accept; no recorded value is ever rewritten." and "the recorded `pending_human_revision.predecessor_input_fingerprint` pair ... which `boundToDeclaredPredecessor` compares against the evidence's own recorded fingerprint — untouched by this phase."

summary: Phase 1 design (config as an editable input) is complete and review-clean after one revision round. It removes all seven live config byte-pin enforcement points (six comparisons plus the status-side verification), keeps the creation-time digest for provenance only, drops config from the input-fingerprint subject with a retry-once legacy-composition fallback at the three comparing sites (kernel, local envelope, gate-reentry replay validations) so in-flight tasks - including this one - keep their recorded evidence valid, and adds a last-seen config snapshot in task state driving a field-level change notice in status, recorded on every config-reading state commit before prepared-state bytes are derived. Unparseable config stays fail-closed as config-invalid with a repair next action. The same-side review's four accepted findings (sixth resolver caller, multiple state writers, corrected composition-convergence model, injection point inside buildPlan) and the counter-review's one accepted blocker (the gate-reentry seam splits into landing computations that write the new composition and replay validations that must match the recorded one) are all carried into the design; the task design's D2 convergence wording was corrected accordingly. One material risk remains: 19 hand-written files including tests - above the per-phase signal threshold - accepted because each edit is narrow and the phase has no independently verifiable split point. Material risks to weigh: removing fail-closed pinning trades machine-blocked config drift for visibility (accepted deliberately by the PRD's trusted-environment model), and the legacy fallback keeps the old composition load-bearing on the ordinary path for legacy tasks rather than converging on every transaction.
